notes: SHIP v1.14.455 - LOCKED RACK MODE IS A CANONICAL FRONT ELEVATION (owner ruling 2026-08-13). WHAT .454 GOT WRONG, STATED PLAINLY. It locked the camera to the angles setFocus had always targeted - LOCK_YAW 0.10 and LOCK_PITCH 0.08 - and called them canonical. Those are 5.7 degrees of yaw and 4.6 degrees of nose-down pitch, so the locked view was a three-quarter shot held steady: the cabinet leaned, its rails converged, and the neighbour competed with it. Locking the wrong pose is not the same as having a canonical one, and the owner was right that nudging one set of world coordinates until one rack looked acceptable would not have fixed the model. THREE MORE FAULTS IN THE SAME FUNCTION. The eye carried a bare plus 0.4 on y with NO matching target offset, so the view axis tilted downward even at pitch zero and the rails could never project as vertical. The look target was camX comma RH times 0.5 comma 0 - the eased camera x plus the hardcoded AISLE ORIGIN - which is derivation from world origin rather than from the rack. And the field of view was 46 degrees, a cinematic aisle lens on what is an inspection surface. THE MODEL NOW. The pose is solved from the SELECTED RACK and nothing else, every frame: target is the rack world centre from getWorldPosition, the normal is 0 comma 0 comma 1 through getWorldQuaternion so a rotated slot would still be read square, and position is target plus normal times distance. Camera up is world up and lookAt targets the centre, giving yaw zero, pitch zero and roll zero by construction. Because position y equals target y the axis is HORIZONTAL, which is the entire reason vertical rails project as vertical lines and cross-members as horizontal ones. It reads nothing from the previous camera, the previous rack, accumulated pan, orbit state, or the aisle origin. THE USABLE VIEWPORT IS MEASURED, NEVER A CONSTANT. The canvas is not the visible area: the scene-utility rail hangs into its top right and the bottom control stack covers its foot, so centring on the raw canvas centre leaves the cabinet visibly shifted. lockUsableRect reads both from the DOM at the moment of use, because the header has no height token and the bottom stack changes height with the status row - 13544 already records what happens when that clearance is written down as a number. setViewOffset then slides the PROJECTION so the optical centre lands on the usable centre. Recentring this way rather than by moving the camera sideways is the whole point: moving it would reintroduce the exact yaw the mode exists to remove. The same mechanism buys headroom for the label with zero degrees of pitch, and the distance is derived from that rect too, so chrome eating the canvas makes the camera step BACK instead of cropping the cabinet. A DEFECT FOUND BY MEASUREMENT INSIDE THIS SHIP. The first cut snapped the ease on TOTAL 3D distance. Every rack shares the same canonical y and z and only x differs, so the large x delta of a rack change held the whole vector above the threshold and y and z never snapped - camera height crept 1.8869 then 1.8971 then 1.89925 across a walk, a height that depended on how many racks you had visited. Snapping PER AXIS fixed it: y and z are exact within a frame or two and stay exact, and only x is ever in flight. The rig slides along a rail. The first lock is also instant now rather than eased, because Forge opening must PRESENT the canonical pose, not glide into it from wherever the camera was constructed. MEASURED, at the real iPhone viewport of 390 by 844. Four racks: s1:010 at minus 4.70, s1:001 at minus 2.35, s4:100 at 0, s4:099 at plus 2.35 - every one of them at y 1.9 and z 10.32353 with forward 0 comma 0 comma minus 1 and roll 0. Navigating s1:010 to s1:001 to s4:100 to s4:099 and back returns to minus 4.70 comma 1.9 comma 10.32353, bit-identical. Vertical framing was corrected from a measurement and not by eye: at LOCK_BIAS_Y 0.06 the shot came back with 63px of slack above the label and 16px below the feet in a 620px usable band, so the cabinet stood on the bottom edge with its base under the hint text. 0.023 splits the slack about evenly at 40 above and 25 below. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. Orthographic was allowed by the ruling but not taken: it would thread a second camera type through RackEngine, the light rig and the fog, all of which sit under RACK SCENE LOCK where only the camera term is open. A 34 degree perspective already yields square verticals because the axis is exactly horizontal and centred, and the remaining convergence is on the NEIGHBOURS, which is honest depth rather than distortion of the selected rack. No second renderer was introduced. RUNS (phone-webkit, each spec ALONE): 37 locked-rack-pose, 36 forge-rack-centric, 02 build-forge, 08 forge-layout. GATES: three-stamp lockstep at .455, inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, brace balance, 0 bare LF. DEVICE-VERIFY: open the aisle and walk several racks. PASS is every cabinet arriving dead straight and centred, rails vertical, top horizontal, no lean, the neighbour clearly subordinate, the full rack and its label and feet in frame, and the same framing on every rack with no drift. FAIL is any lean or off-axis skew, the rack sitting left of centre under the control rail, a neighbour competing for attention, or the framing changing as you walk.
